title: Ending AI Slop — Thais Castello Branco, Taste Labs
talk_summary: A taste/design data company argues subjective domains are hard because they lack measurability and because models collapse to the mean; their fix is decomposing fuzzy goals into codified, verifiable components and routing each component to the right judge (deterministic check, LLM judge, or human expert). They also stress high-quality, specific, expert-labeled data over volume, and treating disagreement as signal rather than noise.

takeaways.technique: Decompose fuzzy review criteria into codified, checkable components
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of asking a judge 'is this good/on-brand', they break the target into explicit elements (colors, typography, spacing, motion) so each can be verified against a ground truth rather than judged holistically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: once you start picking apart the exact elements that represent what great is, then it suddenly becomes the shape of something that is codifiable and verifiable

takeaways.technique: Route each sub-problem to the cheapest adequate judge
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat fuzzy problems as a routing problem: split into components and pick the best method per component (deterministic check, LLM judge, or human), pulling things toward verification where possible.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how do we break down this problem into something that you understand what's actually the best method to solve it

takeaways.technique: Codify ground truth from existing artifacts instead of LLM-judge-only
takeaways.what_they_do: They derive verifiable ground truth from existing decomposable artifacts (e.g. a brand spec) and grade new output against that ground truth, not against replication of the original.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that decomposition that I mentioned becomes the ground truth

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat specificity of an expert's language and its tie to a concrete artifact (e.g. exact code component) as the property that correlates with high-signal data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The specificity of their language and of how precise they're being able to be with how they're doing that description is what will determine that data quality

takeaways.technique: Treat reviewer disagreement as signal, not noise
takeaways.what_they_do: They distinguish disagreement on objective fundamentals (a flaw) from disagreement on subjective style (good data showing real preference differences), and use consensus intentionally.
They argue high-quality, deliberately-selected expert data beats large noisy datasets, and that selection/decomposition is fully controllable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: quality over quantity approach ... creating high quality data is expensive ... yield far better results than getting a bunch of noisy data
